source.title: On the birational section conjecture with strong birationality assumptions
source.version: Published open-access PDF, 22 pages, online 26 September 2023; all pp.129–150 reread by codex-hjdg0j on 22 September 2026. arXiv:2108.13397v3 (15 September 2023) checked at the six source-issue passages; its SHA-256 is e23989fbac0cb38646d34a69f8c724611fd1f46a371122197e25f83f18cbb722. All22 published pages reread by codex-c83e7a on2026-09-23; identical published SHA-256. The v3 passage comparison remains attributed to codex-hjdg0j. All 22 published pages independently reread by codex-a71f92 on 2026-09-23; same SHA-256. No new full reading of older auxiliary references is implied. Independent reviewer Codex codex-7e92bd read all22 published pages on2026-09-23 and compared the six main-paper finding passages with arXivv3; same PDF hashes.
readSections: Entire published pp.129–150: introduction, §§2–7, Lemmas1–26, TheoremsA–C, all proofs, footnote1, acknowledgements and references.

summary: Independent review completed with verdict revise. The published Theorems A–C and all 179 inherited items were checked; a generic analytic inverse library item is added. The extraction retains the explicitly qualified reverse implication of Theorem A: the nonsplit quadratic-boundary case over fields of positive transcendence degree is unresolved here. The number-field replacement and split-completion proof pass this mathematical review relative to their named suppliers. Generic weights and semiabelian Tate modules are reassigned to their shared owners. Twenty version-scoped source findings are confirmed, four already corrected in later publications. No Lean formalisation is claimed.

items.name: Curve and smooth completion
items.statement: A curve is a smooth geometrically connected curve over a characteristic-zero field k; barX is its smooth proper completion. Hyperbolic means 2g(barX)-2+deg(barX\X)>0.
items.note: Planning API and tests: Track geometric connectedness, genus, boundary and base change; test P1, Gm, and P1 minus three points.

items.name: Galois section class
items.statement: S_X/k is the set of continuous right inverses of π1(X)→Gal(k), modulo conjugation by π1(X_bar k).
items.note: Planning API and tests: Representatives, quotient invariance, pushforward and base change; test the rational-point section and a tangential section.

items.name: Geometric sections
items.statement: A point x∈X(k) induces a section class by functoriality; a section is geometric when it belongs to this image.
items.note: Planning API and tests: Naturality and conjugacy independence; test X=Spec k and two distinct points on a hyperbolic curve.

items.name: Cuspidal packet
items.statement: For x∈(barX\X)(k), the packet P_X,x is the image of sections of its local decomposition-group extension in S_X/k; a section is cuspidal if it lies in one of these packets.
items.note: Planning API and tests: Use a henselian punctured neighborhood, inertia and tangential splittings; distinguish the cusp from a choice of section in its packet; test the three cusps of P1 minus three points.

items.name: Birational section
items.statement: S_k(X)/k consists of continuous sections Gal(k(X))→Gal(k), modulo geometric-kernel conjugacy. A cuspidal birational section factors through a decomposition group over a k-rational point of barX.
items.note: Planning API and tests: Generic-to-open restriction and packets; a rational point inside X still gives a cuspidal FUNCTION-FIELD section.

items.name: Birationally liftable section
items.statement: A section s∈S_X/k is b.l. precisely when it is in the image S_k(X)/k→S_X/k.
items.note: Planning API and tests: Witness and restriction API; use this definition, which differs from Stix book Definition 266. Do not replace lifting by a local condition.

items.name: t-birationally liftable section
items.statement: A section s∈S_X/k is t-b.l. precisely when s_k(t) is b.l. over the rational-function extension k(t).
items.note: Planning API and tests: Base-change witness and renaming variable; test rational-point and cuspidal sections. Never infer transcendental base change of arbitrary birational sections.

items.name: Section conjecture proposition
items.statement: For every hyperbolic curve over every field finitely generated over Q, every Galois section is geometric or cuspidal.
items.note: Planning API and tests: A named proposition, with no proof assumption in unconditional endpoints; preserve field and hyperbolicity quantifiers. Independent review: NC.6 is an export/frontier process layer, not a promise of this quantified proposition. Route the residual definition with the birational-sections continuation; no proof of the conjecture is asserted.
items.reviewNote: Corrected in place by REV-PAPER-BRESCIANI-24; see independentReview.changes and the review report.

items.name: Birational section conjecture proposition
items.statement: For every smooth geometrically connected curve over every field finitely generated over Q, every birational section is cuspidal.
items.note: Planning API and tests: Quantify over curves and fields; distinguish the conjecture from the t-b.l. theorem.

items.name: Cuspidalization conjecture proposition
items.statement: For every hyperbolic X over a field finitely generated over Q and every nonempty open U⊆X, the restriction S_U/k→S_X/k is surjective.
items.note: Planning API and tests: Universal open-subset quantifier; test composition of restrictions. This is a conjecture, not an available lifting theorem.

items.name: Nonintegrality places
items.statement: For a birational section z of a smooth projective curve over a number field and nonempty open U with an integral model outside finite S, N_U is the set of places where its associated local point fails to lie in U(O_v).
items.note: Planning API and tests: Model changes alter N_U only by finitely many places; distinguish infinitude, positive Dirichlet density, and density zero.

items.name: Nonintegrality independence
items.statement: The set N_U is independent of the chosen finite-type integral model up to finitely many places; thus its Dirichlet-density question is independent of that model.
items.note: Spread the two models over a common open arithmetic base.

items.name: Stix density alternative
items.statement: For a b.l. section of a hyperbolic curve over a number field, either its associated adelic point is integral on a set of finite places of Dirichlet density one or the section is cuspidal.
items.locator: Published paper §1 p.130; Lemmas 16,20 cite [21] Theorem B
items.note: Read Stix arXiv:1203.3236v3 p.1 Theorem B. Density one does not mean all but finitely many places.

items.name: Stix totally real or imaginary quadratic input
items.statement: For a hyperbolic curve over a totally real or imaginary quadratic number field, every birationally adelic noncuspidal section is geometric.
items.note: Exact source theorem read at Stix p.1. Bresciani’s claim that some N_U is infinite uses this plus deleting an associated rational point; it is not an unconditional all-number-field result.

items.name: Birationally adelic section
items.statement: For a hyperbolic X over a number field with function field K, a section s∈S_X/k is birationally adelic if it has a birational lift z∈S_K/k such that for EVERY nonempty open U⊆X, the induced section on U is either adelic for U/k or cuspidal. An adelic section is a Selmer section whose associated modified adelic point lies in U(A_k)_bullet (integral outside finitely many places, with connected components at infinity).
items.locator: Published paper §1 p.130, input [21] Theorem A
items.note: Planning API and tests: retain existence of ONE birational lift working for all opens and the per-open disjunction; distinguish density-one integrality from adelic integrality. Stix arXiv:1203.3236v3 §2.2.2–§2.2.3 p.4 read.

items.name: Curve family
items.statement: X→V is a family of curves when X=barX\D, barX→V is smooth proper with geometrically connected one-dimensional fibers, and D is a relative divisor finite étale over V.
items.note: Planning API and tests: Base change, empty boundary and fiber; test constant punctured P1 families and a boundary collision that fails étaleness.

items.name: Relative π1 section
items.statement: For a family X→V over an affine curve, a π1 section is a continuous splitting π1(V)→π1(X), modulo conjugation by the geometric-fiber group.
items.note: Planning API and tests: Specialization at v∈V(k), conjugacy independence and shrinking V; test a constant section of a product.

items.name: Power-quotient completion of an abelian group
items.statement: For abelian A, Ahat=lim over positive n of A/nA, with transition maps for divisibility. For multiplicative groups use A/A^n.
items.note: Planning API and tests: Projection, induced maps, separatedness hypotheses and compatibility with valuation; compare Zhat and completion of k*. Infinite direct sums do not become unrestricted products. A/nA need not be finite. This inverse limit must not be identified with the ordinary profinite completion used in /136 without additional hypotheses.

items.name: fpqc and fppf sites
items.statement: The fpqc topology is generated by jointly surjective quasi-compact flat covering families; fppf uses flat locally finitely presented covers.
items.note: Planning API and tests: Use existing sites and inclusion; test fppf≤fpqc. Do not construct new sites for torsors.

items.name: Stack descent framework
items.statement: A category-valued pseudofunctor on a site is a stack if it is a prestack and descent data for covering sieves are effective.
items.note: Planning API and tests: Reuse IsStack and effective descent equivalence; test a trivial cover. This does not claim a geometric gerbe implementation.

items.name: Finite and profinite étale gerbes
items.statement: A finite étale gerbe over k is an étale gerbe with finite geometric automorphism groups; a profinite étale gerbe is a cofiltered 2-limit of such gerbes.
items.note: Planning API and tests: Isomorphism groupoids, neutralizations, band and finite-stage presentation; test BG for a finite constant group and inverse limits.

items.name: Classifying stack of a group scheme
items.statement: B_kG assigns to a k-scheme S the groupoid of fpqc G_S-torsors. For finite-type G the fppf topology suffices; retain fpqc for profinite G.
items.note: Planning API and tests: Pullback, trivial torsor, automorphism group, equivalence under group-scheme isomorphism; test μ_n and Zhat(1).

items.name: Étale fundamental gerbe
items.statement: For the geometrically connected schemes in the paper, X→Π_X/k is universal for maps from X to finite étale stacks, and Π_X/k is a profinite étale gerbe.
items.note: Planning API and tests: Universal equivalence on Hom groupoids, functoriality, comparison to IG.0’s finite-cover fiber functor; test Spec k, A1 and Gm.

items.name: Sections as gerbe points
items.statement: The isomorphism classes of Π_X/k(k) identify with S_X/k, compatibly with rational points, functoriality and conjugacy.
items.note: Use the actual groupoid comparison, not equality of bare cardinalities.

items.name: Pointed fundamental group scheme
items.statement: Given x∈X(k), descend the continuous Gal(k)-action on π1(X_bar k,x) to an étale profinite group scheme π1(X,x). There is a neutralization Π_X/k≃B_kπ1(X,x).
items.note: Planning API and tests: Track choice of x and twisting by its torsor; test trivial torsor and a change of rational point.

items.name: Fundamental gerbe base change
items.statement: In characteristic zero, for a geometrically connected concentrated fibered category X and any extension k′/k, Π_(X_k′)/k′≃Π_X/k×k k′. In particular this applies to the paper’s curves and k(t).
items.locator: Published paper §2 p.133 and p.135, citation [6] A.18
items.note: CORRECTED LOCATOR: [6] published Proposition A.23, p.264, read; A.18 p.262 only proves algebraic separable extensions. Concentration and char 0 are retained.

items.name: Family homotopy exact sequence
items.statement: Let k have characteristic zero, A be a localization of a one-dimensional regular finite-type k-domain, C=Spec A, and X→C a family of curves. For a geometric fiber F, 1→π1(F)→π1(X)→π1(C)→1 is exact.
items.note: Proof uses complex affine-curve π2=0, exactness of profinite completion for the specified curve groups, descent to C, and limits of finite étale covers. Do not generalize to arbitrary proper bases.

items.name: Complex affine-curve asphericity input
items.statement: A smooth connected affine complex curve has the homotopy type of a finite wedge of circles, hence π2=0 and finitely generated free π1. For a locally trivial topological curve family over it, the homotopy sequence is short exact on π1; the fiber group is finitely generated.
items.note: The curve-topology/Riemann-existence and locally trivial family comparisons remain IG.1 proof obligations. Completion now uses /29 and /140–/145, not the unread Anderson theorem or cohomological goodness. A group-theoretic splitting does not assert a geometric section of the family.

items.name: Completion exactness input for curve families
items.statement: For the complex affine-base topological curve-family extension 1→N→G→F_r→1 in Lemma1, N is finitely generated and F_r is free; therefore 1→hat N→hat G→hat F_r→1 is split exact as profinite groups.
items.locator: Published Lemma1 p.134; replacement proof in this continuation, using /140–/145; independently Bekka, arXiv:2305.04803v1, CorollaryC p.4.
items.note: CLOSED SOURCE GAP BY REPLACEMENT, not a claim to have read Anderson. Lift free generators to split the abstract extension; characteristic finite-index subgroups of N provide cofinal finite quotient restrictions from G. The completion universal property gives right exactness and extends the splitting. No residual-finiteness or goodness assumption is needed; finite generation of N and splitting are essential to this proof. Generic completion lemma belongs only to ProfiniteProPGroupsPartIISplitCompletion; IG.1 owns this geometric application.

items.name: Limit of finite étale covers
items.statement: For C a localization of a finite-type regular affine curve, finite étale covers descend to an open neighborhood U, giving π1(C)≃lim_U π1(U); the analogous assertion holds for the spread-out family.
items.note: Record filtered descent and eventual equality of morphisms; constant left term identifies the inverse-limit extension.

items.name: Relative fundamental gerbe
items.statement: Π_X/C is the 2-fiber product C×_(Π_C/k)Π_X/k, with its natural map X→Π_X/C over C.
items.note: Planning API and tests: 2-cartesian universal property, sections and base change; test constant families.

items.name: Relative fiber comparison
items.statement: Under Lemma 1 hypotheses, for every field extension k′/k and c:Spec k′→C, Π_(X_c)/k′→Π_X/C×_C Spec k′ is an isomorphism.
items.note: Requires /26’s arbitrary-extension base change and /27’s full exactness, not just right exactness.

items.name: Proper étale relative-gerbe presentation
items.statement: Π_X/C→C is a cofiltered limit of proper étale relative gerbes Φ_i→C.
items.note: Present source and target by finite étale gerbes with locally full transition maps and set Φ_i=Ψ_i×_(Ξ_i)C.

items.name: Locally full morphism of gerbes
items.statement: For affine gerbes over k, a morphism is locally full when the induced automorphism-group map at every field-valued object is faithfully flat; equivalently the maps of fpqc Isom sheaves are surjective. On neutral finite étale geometric fibers this is surjectivity of finite band groups.
items.note: Definition3.4 and Proposition3.10 read directly, published pp.538–540. Planning API/tests: composition, fpqc base change and neutral BG→BH comparison; test a surjection, a proper subgroup inclusion and identity. Scheme-theoretic faithful flatness is primary, not surjectivity on k-rational points.

items.name: Locally full finite étale gerbes are relative gerbes
items.statement: A locally full morphism of finite étale gerbes over k is a proper étale relative gerbe.
items.locator: Bresciani Lemma2 p.135; Borne–Vistoli2019 Proposition3.10 pp.540–541.
items.note: Exact affine-gerbe criterion read: locally full iff relative gerbe. For finite étale gerbes, after an fpqc neutralizing cover the fiber is B ker(G→H), with finite étale kernel, hence proper and étale; descend those properties. Presentation by locally full projections is split into /149 rather than bundled here. The proof text of Prop3.10 mislabels its factorization implications as (1)⇒(3)/(3)⇒(1); their argument concerns condition(4), not a change of theorem.

items.name: Finite root stack of a DVR
items.statement: For DVR R with uniformizer π, the nth root stack of its closed divisor classifies triples (L,s,α:L^n≃O) with α(s^n)=π; it is [Spec R[t]/(t^n−π)/μ_n].
items.note: Planning API and tests: Prove independence of uniformizer, transition maps when n divides m, generic isomorphism and reduced closed fiber Bμ_n. Test n=1.

items.name: Infinite root stack and specializing circle
items.statement: The infinite root stack is lim_n root_n(Spec R). Its reduced closed fiber S_c^1 is noncanonically B_k Zhat(1); its k-point isomorphism classes are noncanonically H1(k,Zhat(1))=completed k*.
items.note: Planning API and tests: Distinguish stack from set of isomorphism classes and choice-free object from chosen neutralization; test a change of uniformizer.

items.name: Constant gerbe morphism
items.statement: A morphism Y→X of fibered categories over k is constant if it factors through Spec k.
items.note: Planning API and tests: Factorization witnesses and invariance under equivalence; test a trivial group homomorphism and a nontrivial map Bμ_n→Bμ_n.

items.name: Tame stack valuative input
items.statement: For a tame proper morphism of algebraic stacks X→Y, a DVR R with fraction field K, and a compatible generic lift Spec K→X over Spec R→Y, there is a unique positive n and a representable lift root_n(Spec R)→X; the lift is unique up to a unique compatible isomorphism.
items.note: Primary arXiv:2210.03406v1 pp.3–4 read. The representability condition is essential for uniqueness of n; no residue-field extension is needed.

items.name: Extension to infinite root stack
items.statement: For the curve family and closed point of Proposition 3, a generic section z extends uniquely up to a unique compatible isomorphism from Spec K to the infinite root stack of the local DVR.
items.note: Apply the proper tame criterion at each finite gerbe stage and pass to the limit; uniqueness is relative to the specified generic datum.

items.name: Specializing loop
items.statement: The specializing loop γ_z(c):S_c^1→Π_(X_c)/k(c) is the restriction of the infinite-root-stack extension of z to the reduced closed fiber.
items.note: Planning API and tests: Functoriality, finite-level compatibility and base change; test Gm and valuation-zero versus nonzero sections.

items.name: Unramified extension criterion
items.statement: The generic section extends over Spec R if and only if its specializing loop is constant.
items.note: Retain R and the relative gerbe from the proposition; use the fixed generic datum in uniqueness.

items.name: Possibly nonunique specialization
items.statement: A specialization of z at c is a section class in the essential image of γ_z(c) evaluated on k(c)-points.
items.note: Planning API and tests: Existence, pushforward and field-base-change compatibility; specialize the chosen trivial torsor after a neutralization.

items.name: Existence and one-way uniqueness
items.statement: Specializations always exist. If the specializing loop is constant then the specialization is unique.
items.note: Split from the false converse; existence uses rational points of S_c^1 after a uniformizer choice.

items.name: Automorphism criterion for constancy
items.statement: For a chosen s∈S_c^1(k(c)), γ_z(c) is constant iff Aut(s)=Zhat(1)→Aut(γ_z(c)(s)) is trivial. Consequently constancy can be checked after algebraic closure of the constant field.
items.note: Retain descent compatibility; triviality of geometric band map is stronger than cardinality-one image on rational points.

items.name: Henselian specialization by a uniformizer
items.statement: Choose compatible roots of a uniformizer in the henselization R^h. They split Gal(K^h)→Gal(k), and composing that splitting with a generic section and specialization π1(X_Rh)≃π1(X_k) yields a specialization.
items.note: Planning API and tests: Track root choices, decomposition subgroup and inertia I≃Zhat(1); recover the gerbe construction. Characteristic zero of both fields excludes wild inertia here.

items.name: Ramification map and nonabelian H1 image
items.statement: A chosen specialization makes I→π1(X_bar k) Galois equivariant; the set of specializations is its image on nonabelian Galois H1. An unramified section has trivial ramification map.
items.note: Planning API and tests: Twisting action, conjugacy independence and map on torsors; compare constant-loop and unramified notions without assuming injectivity of H1 maps.

items.name: Gm fundamental gerbe and Kummer description
items.statement: The section 1 identifies Π_Gm/R with B_R Zhat(1); its R- and K-point classes are completed R* and completed K* respectively.
items.note: The compact-coefficient Kummer comparison and torsor interpretation are explicit missing adapters.

items.name: Completed valuation
items.statement: A DVR valuation v:K*→Z induces v:completed K*→Zhat. Its kernel is the image of completed R*; the split decomposition K*=R*×π^Z gives the proof.
items.note: Planning API and tests: Evaluation on a uniformizer, compatibility with ramification index and independence of the splitting for v; test v(π)=1.

items.name: Gm loop criterion
items.statement: For a generic Gm section z∈completed K*, its specializing loop is constant iff v(z)=0.
items.note: Uses completed valuation and the extension criterion; no positive-characteristic assertion.

items.name: Unique specialization does not imply constant loop
items.statement: For R=C[x]_(x), the generic Gm section represented by x has nonconstant loop because v(x)=1, but has a unique specialization because H1(C,Zhat(1)) is trivial.
items.note: Required negative unit test for the specialization API.

items.name: Finite local image forces a constant torus loop
items.statement: Let T/k be a torus and ν:k*→Z a surjective valuation. If γ:B_k Zhat(1)→Π_T/k has finitely many isomorphism classes in the image on kν-points of its k-points, then γ is constant.
items.note: Split T over a finite extension k′; the completed valuation surjects onto Zhat. Ramification index r≠0 and torsion-freeness force rf=0⇒f=0.

items.name: Finite local image forces a constant curve loop
items.statement: Let k be a number field, ν a finite place, X/k a curve. If γ:B_k Zhat(1)→Π_X/k has finite image on kν-isomorphism classes of its k-points, then γ is constant.
items.note: Pass to finite étale cover detecting nontriviality in abelianization; use generalized Jacobian, weight separation, Mattuck and Lemma 7.

items.name: Finite-cover abelian detection
items.statement: Let 1→G→E→G_k→1 be the arithmetic fundamental-group sequence of a smooth geometrically connected curve X/k in characteristic zero, s:G_k→E a section, and f:Zhat(1)→G a nontrivial continuous homomorphism equivariant for s. There is an open subgroup E′⊂E containing s(G_k) and f(Zhat(1)), projecting onto G_k, such that f is nonzero in (E′∩G)^ab. Thus the corresponding geometrically connected finite étale cover Y→X has a lift of s and of the loop, with nonconstant abelianized loop.
items.note: Choose a characteristic open subgroup N⊂G detecting f, using finite generation of the geometric curve group. In G/N the image C of f is cyclic and s(G_k)-stable. Let H be its inverse image and E′=H⋊s(G_k). Then H→C is an abelian quotient detecting f. The finite-fiber map on section classes preserves the finite local-image condition. This makes the arithmetic descent and the neutralizing object explicit; no rational point is chosen.

items.name: Finite fibers under finite étale covers
items.statement: For a finite étale morphism Y→X, the map of section classes has finite fibers, so finite-image conditions survive passage to a suitable section neighborhood.
items.note: Use cosets of the finite-index fundamental subgroup; isolate any finite constant-field extension needed.

items.name: Semiabelian Jacobian and Albanese torsor
items.statement: For a smooth open curve X with completion and reduced boundary, construct its generalized Jacobian J, an extension 1→T→J→A→1 with A the proper Jacobian, together with the degree-one Albanese torsor when no rational base point is given.
items.note: Planning API and tests: Keep torsor and group distinct; test proper curves T=0, Gm with J=Gm, and a curve without a rational point.

items.name: Tate module of a semiabelian variety
items.statement: For J as above, TJ=lim_n J[n] on geometric points with its profinite Galois action; 0→TT→TJ→TA→0 is the torsion-limit extension.
items.note: Planning API and tests: Compare all-prime and primewise modules, base change, exactness and π1(J_bar k); test Gm giving Zhat(1). General semiabelian torsion and its all-prime Tate extension are supplied once by C4, importing A3/A4 and compact inverse-limit exactness; the generalized Jacobian is a consumer.
items.reviewNote: Corrected in place by REV-PAPER-BRESCIANI-24; see independentReview.changes and the review report.

items.name: Abelianized fundamental gerbe comparison
items.statement: Let X/k be a smooth geometrically connected curve in characteristic zero, J its generalized Jacobian and P its generalized Albanese torsor, with a:X→P. The induced map Π_X/k^ab→Π_P/k is an equivalence of gerbes banded by TJ. Given s∈Π_X/k(k), its images s_ab and a(s) neutralize these gerbes, giving (Π_X/k^ab,s_ab)≃(B_k TJ,*)≃(Π_P/k,a(s)). In particular the loop γ:B_k Zhat(1)→Π_X/k of Lemma 8, with s=γ(*), induces a Galois-equivariant homomorphism Zhat(1)→TJ. Neither X(k) nor P(k) is assumed nonempty.
items.locator: Published paper Lemma 8 p.138; Harari–Szamuely, author bash5.pdf, §1 and Remark 2.4; Bresciani 1904.00789v2, Lemma 5.8
items.note: Comparison resolved from /150 (geometric isomorphism), /151 (canonical band of a semiabelian torsor), and /152 (neutralization by a chosen gerbe object). Equivalence is checked after separable base change; commutativity makes the band descent independent of translations. The section does not trivialize P as a J-torsor. This repairs the missing choice in the printed canonical identification; see sourceIssue E4 and the report. Routed once to JacobianChallengePartIIGeneralizedAlbanese.

items.name: Weight vanishing for abelian Tate modules
items.statement: For an abelian variety A over a number field, every Galois-equivariant homomorphism Zhat(1)→TA is zero.
items.locator: Published paper Lemma 8 p.138; input [7] Lemma 3.3 read
items.note: Use primewise weight −2 versus −1 at good finite places and injectivity into rational Tate modules; import actual purity results, not merely a weight label. DWP.0/DWP.1 supply disjoint-weight Hom vanishing and the abelian Weil estimate. Import R01.6 good-reduction realization and A4; for each ℓ choose a good finite place of residue characteristic different from ℓ, then descend from rational vanishing using torsion-freeness.
